newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday, September 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday, September 23.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro comments on the new corruption scandal involving state railway managing director Lorenzo Necci:"another serious injury has been opened". Magistrates should "use the scalpel to save the healthy part of the country" (all).
* Massimo D'Alema, leader of the Democratic party of the Left, warns Fausto Bertinotti over the 1997 budget: "It's not time for vetos or ultimatums". "Out of Europe Italy would break up" (Corriere).
* Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi insists over cuts in the pension funds and in the health system for the 1997 budget (all).
* The number of public employees is decreasing: in 1995 12 sample ministers were employing 139.981 people, 3.800 less than in 1993 (Sole).
* Antonio D'Amato, head of Southern Italy policy at Confindustria says the Mezzogiorno is a powder-keg, with unemployement at a danger level" (Repubblica).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
